title: Pocket Flock - Centre for Digital Media project for Buffalo Buffalo
description: A cozy mobile idle collection game about birdwatching built in Unity for client Buffalo Buffalo as a Centre for Digital Media project. The goal was to create an experience resembling having a bird sanctuary in your pocket, where players discover birds, create postcards with bird photos, decorate, and manage light progression mechanics. It took 3 months to go from ideation to polished prototype.
thingsLearned: How to architect modular systems in Unity for mobile, working with a cross-discipline team of designers, artists and developers, and preparing a product from ideation to prototype.
approach: I served as development lead, designing the core system architecture and data structures while actively contributing to game design. We iterated rapidly using Agile/Kanban to keep art and development pipelines synchronized under a strict deadline.
challengesAndResults: Ensuring core modular systems interacted seamlessly without data loss or major bugs was a big challenge, but we manage to delivered a polished, functional prototype that received full stakeholder approval.
approachDetailed: As the lead developer, I was responsible for turning abstract game design concepts into clean, maintainable Unity code. I structured the project around modular managers and Scriptable Objects to separate game data (like bird stats and progression triggers) from the presentation layer. Since we had a multidisciplinary team, we worked with clear Kanban workflows and pipeline standards so every team member was able to see the progress of the prototype. I also drafted technical specs and rapidly iterated on state machine logic, keeping our sprint velocity high.
challengesAndResultsDetailed: The main challenge was maintaining the core modular systems interacting with each other with no loss of data or major bugs, while managing unique collection assets without hardcoding values and ensuring touch menus scaled across different smartphone resolutions. To solve this, I architected a data-driven system using Scriptable Objects and JSON serialization so designers could tweak variables independently, while building dynamic anchor-based UI layouts and custom state controllers. As a result, we delivered a polished, functional client-approved vertical slice on time that met all stakeholder requirements and established a solid code framework.
thingsLearnedDetailed: I learned how to architect modular systems in Unity for mobile, while working with a cross-discipline team of designers, artists, and developers. I gained experience structuring Unity projects specifically for touch interfaces, responsive UI, and efficient data serialization. Through technical leadership, I managed technical scope, maintained a functioning GitHub repository with version control, and wrote clear technical documentation for handoffs. Additionally, I deepened my understanding of idle progression loops, tuning variables so player feedback felt satisfying without breaking the underlying pacing.

title: Bumigumi Magic Trails - Centre for Digital Media project for Bumigumi
description: A mobile AR narrative game prototype created for Bumigumi as a Centre for Digital Media project. The project combined real-time camera tracking, vision-based interactions, and story progression to create an immersive augmented reality experience for children to explore Stanley Park. I worked as the developer lead in gameplay scripting, game design, build testing, and feature iteration to help bring the concept to life. It took 3 months to go from ideation to polished prototype.
thingsLearned: I developed a deep understanding of how real-time tracking systems and vision frameworks interact with Unity's frame lifecycle and hardware limitations. I learned how gameplay mechanics work for AR games on mobile, including AI image recognition and motion tracking, while using Yarn Spinner to ensure dialogue worked and was easy to change on each iteration. Working together with the client to bring a vertical slice and a live demonstration to life also taught me how to manage client expectations, bridging production goals with tight deadlines.
approach: My focus was on bridging gameplay scripting with physical, vision-based mechanics in Unity. I helped design interactive moments, managed GitHub source control for clean repository health, drafted technical specs for the client and iterated on mechanics rapidly to test game interactivity with exploration outdoors. I also took ownership of build inspection, regularly testing functional builds on actual target mobile hardware to catch bugs and performance dips.
challengesAndResults: The primary challenge was managing multiple types of AR interactions with different scopes through fast-paced sprints. I addressed this by rapidly iterating on proposed interactions, testing their feasibility, and polishing the selected interactions to develop the final versions for each section of the game. As a result, we delivered a stable, highly functional prototype that was successfully used in client fundraising demonstrations.

title: Final Stand - Unreal Engine course project
description: A Blackjack game built in Unreal Engine that pits players against a custom AI opponent with the use of powerups, inspired by Buckshot Roulette. Built as a deep dive into engine architecture, the project focuses on separating underlying game rules from visual presentation by pairing native C++ with Unreal Blueprints. This was made as a solo project for an Unreal Engine course in 4 weeks.
thingsLearned: I learned how to expose C++ data and logic to Blueprints using macros like UFUNCTION and UPROPERTY, ensuring native code handles rules while Blueprints handle visual polish. I learned how to construct a clean finite state machine to drive the opponent AI's turn decisions. Furthermore, I discovered how simple timeline animations, camera framing, and audio cues transform a basic turn-based card game into an experience that feels far more polished.
approach: I scoped this project around learning Unreal's hybrid workflow. I wrote the core rules, card shuffling, deck evaluation, and AI decision logic entirely in C++. Then, I exposed those C++ functions to Blueprints, using visual scripting strictly for UI dynamic updates, card animation timelines, and sound effects. This kept the code clean, modular, and fast. I focused on functionality, while also interacting with the 3D elements on the scene.
challengesAndResults: The main challenge was preventing asynchronous timing bugs between C++ card evaluations and Blueprint visual animations, such as making sure each hand wasn't evaluated before the dealing finished. To fix this, I implemented event-driven delegates in C++ that broadcasted state changes only when animation timelines signaled completion. As a result, I built a fully functional, bug-free Unreal prototype in 4 weeks that demonstrated clean engine architecture and responsive UI design.

title: Useless Vending Machine - Big Mode Game Jam 2026
description: A quirky, short-loop solo game created in 3 days for the Big Mode Game Jam 2026. The player interacts with a completely unhelpful vending machine to buy an elusive product. The project was an exercise in aggressive scope management, humor, and leveraging custom sound design to create a memorable game feel.
thingsLearned: I learned the art of aggressive scope management and cutting features early to ensure the core loop remains tight, feels polished, and has minimal bugs. I realized how much weight custom audio carries in making simple interactions feel physical and funny. Additionally, executing this project solo taught me to manage time, interaction mechanics, and asset pipelines independently under a hard 72-hour deadline.
approach: Knowing I only had 3 days, I scoped the project down to a single screen and a tight interaction loop. Instead of spending hours on art or complex physics, I focused on high-polish interaction and custom audio design. I recorded all sound effects using my own voice, aligning them closely with physics impacts and button presses to create a more comical, responsive experience.
challengesAndResults: The challenge was making a static, single-object mechanic feel dynamic and fun over multiple interactions without feature bloat. I solved this by using random pitch variations, subtle camera shakes, and unexpected sound triggers to keep every click surprising. Ultimately, I submitted a polished, humorous jam entry that stood out for its unique audio design.

title: Neil-A's Big Halloween - Global Game Jam 2026
description: A story-driven narrative game made in 72 hours with a team of 7 for Global Game Jam 2026 around the theme 'Mask'. The game follows a lost alien trying to find his brother on Halloween party at night, through dialogue choices and character interactions.
thingsLearned: I learned how to set up Yarn Spinner in Unity to manage branching dialogue, story variables, and UI text boxes. Working in a large team of 7 gave me experience in quick alignment and delegating tasks across different skill levels under tight jam constraints. Through this process, I gained a clear understanding of how to decouple narrative content creation from core engine logic.
approach: With two dedicated writers producing a massive amount of text, our team integrated Yarn Spinner into Unity. I helped structure the dialogue nodes and variable triggers, ensuring our team could push text, character portraits, and branching choices directly into the game without requiring custom code for every line.
challengesAndResults: The main challenge was integrating a massive amount of last-minute narrative content on day 3 without breaking existing event triggers or dialogue flow. I solved this by building modular dialogue triggers that read variable states dynamically, allowing writers to tweak dialogue without creating bugs. As a result, we completed a charming, dialogue-heavy narrative game on time, featuring full branching paths and custom UI.

title: A Disadvantageous Adventure - Solo project
description: An incremental mobile prototype made in Unity about rolling dice to defeat enemies. It was developed to explore mobile development, progression balancing and dice mechanics. Created as a personal proof-of-concept while preparing for mobile development pipelines, it combines touch inputs, scaling upgrade math, and physical dice rolls.
thingsLearned: I learned to use Unity's Input System to handle touch gestures and mouse interactions simultaneously. Applying my background in Operations Research, I used mathematical modeling to balance incremental multipliers, cost curves, and random dice roll outcomes. Prototyping this personal project allowed me to validate mobile interaction patterns before applying them to larger team projects.
approach: I scoped this project for a strict 2-week development window at the start of the Pocket Flock project. My goal was twofold: learn about mobile development and design a satisfying incremental progression curve. I used my background in Operations Research to balance the upgrade costs against dice probability, ensuring progression felt rewarding.
challengesAndResults: The primary challenge was making physical 2D/3D dice rolls feel natural and tactile rather than like a random number generator hidden behind UI. I solved this by implementing physics-based forces to give weight to every roll. Consequently, I successfully published a playable cross-platform prototype on itch.io that proved out mobile input systems and economy mechanics.

title: Meownshine Express Co. - Game Design course project
description: A cozy management simulation game built in Unity over 2 months with a team of 6 for a Game Design course. This was my very first Unity game project, laying the foundation for my game development journey. It follows a bootlegging cat trying to revive his family legacy growing their crops, brewing booze and delivering to the customers.
thingsLearned: As my very first game project, I built my core foundation in C#, GameObjects, UI Canvas management, and scene organization in Unity. I learned how to collaborate on a shared project with a team of 6, distribute tasks, and present a finished game to an audience. Additionally, I developed an efficient process for learning new game engine features quickly using technical documentation, tutorials, and AI tools.
approach: Starting from scratch, I learned Unity's fundamental concepts, game loops, component architectures, and prefabs, through documentation, technical tutorials, and AI-assisted troubleshooting. Our team brainstormed a cozy simulation concept, created early prototypes to test management loops, and iteratively polished the final submission for our class presentation.
challengesAndResults: The main challenge was learning a complex engine like Unity from scratch while delivering a complete team simulation game on a 2-month deadline. To solve this, I broke mechanics down into smaller script modules, like an inventory script, and tested each before implementing them into the game. As a result, our team successfully built and published my first playable Unity game on itch.io.
